meaning: NVIDIA's code for reconstructing splats. It has a ray-traced method (3DGRT) and a rasterised method (3DGUT).
aarch64 is the 64-bit Arm processor architecture. AWS Graviton and the NVIDIA DGX Spark use it.
An experiment that changes one setting and keeps the others fixed, to measure what that setting contributes.
A job rule that cancels the queued part of a rollout once a set percentage of executions has failed. The rule counts failures only after a minimum number of devices has been notified.
An action whose numbers are the targets themselves.
A small policy. The paper that introduced it also introduced action chunking for robot imitation in its current form.
The output of a policy at one instant. On the SO-101, it is six target joint angles.
Several future actions that one policy call returns. The host plays them one per tick.
Physical Intelligence's name for the action head.
The last part of a policy network, the part that outputs the action chunk.
The list of actions that the robot computer holds and has not played yet. It plays one of them on every tick.
LeRobot's grace period, 1 s by default. When the action queue runs dry, a supported robot holds its last target for this long before the run faults.
The two numbers of a chunked policy: how many actions one call returns, and how many of them the host plays before the policy looks again. In LeRobot's ACT, they are chunk_size and n_action_steps.
The intermediate values that the forward pass computes for each sample. They stay in GPU memory until the backward pass uses them, so they grow with the batch.
The program that runs the current policy on the arm and sends what happened to the learner.
An actuator model that is a neural network trained on hardware data. Isaac Lab uses it in place of an ideal PD loop.
A 2026 loop in which a coding agent first rewrites the instructions, tools and procedure around a frozen VLA, and then fine-tunes only the sub-steps that stay unreliable. It was tested on the SO-101.
The outcome that followed an action minus the outcome that the value function predicted. It measures how much better or worse than expected the attempt went.

A training method that labels each recorded action as better or worse than expected and trains the policy on all of them with the label as an extra input. At run time, the policy is asked for the better label.
The software that runs a language model as a coding agent, such as Codex or Claude Code. The same model can behave differently under different agent programs.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, AWS's managed service for running agents. A session on its microVMs ends after at most 8 hours.

A 2026 preview preprint by a single author. In its loop, a language-model controller owns the measurement and the decision to keep or discard a checkpoint, and a statistical gate decides when a new checkpoint replaces the best one.
The default merge in LeRobot remote inference. It drops incoming actions whose time has passed and replaces only the future part of the queue.
The rule by which Batch chooses an instance type from the list when its first choice is not available.
A workload type. The work never ends, such as video that arrives all day, and it runs on a group of machines that stays up all the time. A lost machine costs only the item it was processing.
The remote-desktop protocol for interactive workstations on EC2.
AWS's managed Kubernetes service. Its best-practices guide gives the checkpoint intervals cited in this section.
The AWS event bus that routes events such as a new S3 object or a Spot notice to targets.
The disk image that an EC2 instance boots from.
The event and formula definitions that Arm publishes for each core, including its top-down formulas and its slots per cycle. Arm publishes no file for the Cortex-A78AE.
Extra inertia at a joint that comes from the spinning motor and its gears.
One AWS Batch submission that creates many child jobs. Each child reads its own index number, for example to pick its random seed.
A file that a component needs on the device, such as a script, a binary or a container image.

expansion: Agentic Skill Programming through Iterative Robot Exploration
meaning: A 2026 loop in which coding agents write robot control programs and train no weights. The agents keep repairs that pass verification as text skills.
A way of scheduling policy calls in which the robot computer starts the next call early, while the current chunk is still playing.
A LeRobot mode that starts the next policy call while the arm is still playing the current chunk. It works only while the remaining actions last longer than the call.
One try at the task. It ends when the policy succeeds, fails or runs out of time. The success rate in section 16 is the share of single attempts that succeed.
One try at the task by the current policy. It is an episode in which the policy drives the arm instead of a person.
The AWS Batch job timeout. A job has no timeout unless you set one, either in the job definition or when you submit the job.
The transformer operation in which one token reads information from other tokens. The action head uses it to read the backbone's results.
To vary a training image, for example with a crop or a colour shift, so that the policy sees more variety.
Turning one recorded episode into many varied copies, so that training has more samples to learn from.
The mechanism that restarts a job after its node was replaced: annotations on a Kubernetes job, or a flag on a Slurm step.
Generating one token at a time, where each token depends on the ones before it.
A video compression format. LeRobot writes its videos in AV1 by default and both writes and reads them with CPU code.
One of the separate groups of data centres inside an AWS Region. EFA traffic cannot cross from one Availability Zone to another.
AWS's managed job queue. It runs each job in a container on instances that it starts.
AWS's managed render farm.
The AWS service that holds the registry of devices and the message broker that the devices connect to.
Software that runs on a device and receives deployments from the cloud. It delivers new versions of the model to the computer next to the arm.
AWS's other way to build a Slurm cluster. Its boot hooks map onto PCS node lifecycle actions.
Managed Slurm: AWS runs the controller, and compute node groups start instances for waiting jobs and can scale back to zero.
The AWS workflow service that orders steps as states and can submit a Batch job and wait for it.
The stages of a core's pipeline that execute micro-operations in the arithmetic and memory units, out of program order when that is faster.
The share of slots left empty because the back end could not accept another micro-operation.
The vision-language model inside a VLA. It turns the camera images and the instruction into tokens and reads them once per call.
The backbone is the large pretrained body of a model. When it is frozen, its weights stay unchanged and only the smaller parts built on top of it are trained.
Free play in a gear train that lets the joint move without the motor turning. For the SO-101's servo, the datasheet allows up to 0.5 degrees.
The gradient computation used in training. Guided RTC runs one at every denoising step.
The share of slots that carried work thrown away after a wrong branch guess. In the corrected formulas, it also includes the slots lost while the core recovers from the wrong guess.
The average of a judge's detection rate on successes and its detection rate on failures. A score of 0.5 means chance.
A way to publish to a reserved $aws/rules/ topic, so that the actions of an AWS IoT rule run on the message without going through the message broker.
The samples that one training step processes. The per-GPU batch is what one GPU holds, and the global batch is the per-GPU batch times the number of GPUs.
Supervised learning on pairs of observation and action taken from demonstrations. The network is trained to output the action that the person took for each observation.
A fixed set of simulated tasks that everyone scores on, so that results can be compared.
The state of a benchmark on which nearly every policy scores near the top, so the score no longer separates good policies from poor ones.
Making N independent attempts and counting a success if any of them succeeds. ENPIRE's retries are not independent, because each retry is made after the previous failure has been seen.
A 16-bit number format that takes 2 bytes per weight.
The term c in the equation of motion. It is the pull of gravity and of the body's own motion.
The five columns that the recorder fills in on every row: timestamp, frame_index, episode_index, index and task_index.
How much idle quota beyond its own allocation a team may use, in percent of that allocation.
The resource that a job runs out of first. It is fully used while the rest of the machine is partly idle, and it tells you which instance type to choose.
A compression method that repeatedly merges pairs of symbols that occur often. Text tokenisers use it.
The first and cheapest phase of collision detection. It picks out the pairs of bodies that could be touching.
A BVH is a tree of nested boxes around the triangles of a scene. A ray tracer walks down this tree to find the first triangle that a ray hits.

A fetch of data into one of the core's caches, the first-level data cache or the second-level cache, from further out in the memory system. The number of refills per thousand instructions shows how heavily a program depends on memory.
Context that the language-model provider has already processed on an earlier call and reads again. It made up about 96% of one ENPIRE agent's tokens.
LeRobot's timing summary of a session. It shows the time that each step of the loop takes and the time that the loop slept per tick.
A one-time step that records the range of each joint, so that raw encoder steps map to the same scale on every arm.
The whole run of ideas toward the goal. A campaign can outlast one agent session.
A small set of devices that receives an update before the rest of the fleet.
One action sequence that a planner tries inside a world model.
A reservation of GPU instances for a fixed window, bought ahead.
A Capacity Block for ML reserves a block of EC2 GPU instances for a fixed period. As of November 2026, the list of supported types holds P and Trainium types and no G type.
GPU instances that you reserve in advance for a fixed period, so that a large run can start on a known date.
The way a cloud machine is bought, which decides whether it can be taken back in the middle of a job.
The purchase option a NodePool allows: spot, on-demand or reserved (capacity reservations).
The record of one program on one core. It holds the program's rate, its four slot shares and its memory stall.
Cartpole is a small standard control task in which a cart balances a pole. Isaac Lab uses it in its benchmark.
A search method that samples candidate action sequences from a Gaussian, keeps the few with the lowest cost and refits the Gaussian to them. It repeats this for several rounds.
A fingerprint of a distribution. For a batch, you estimate it by averaging cos(t p) and sin(t p) over the batch's values p. SIGReg compares it with the characteristic function of a standard Gaussian.
A copy of the model that a training job saves to storage while it runs. A stopped run can restart from it.
A SageMaker HyperPod feature, built on NVIDIA NeMo, that rebuilds a failed node's training state from its healthy peers instead of restarting from a saved checkpoint.
The group of future actions that one policy call returns. In NVIDIA's GR00T N1.7 benchmark, one chunk holds 40 actions. The arm plays these actions one at a time while the next call runs.
A numbered folder, such as chunk-000, that holds up to 1,000 data or video files by default.
PPO's limit on how far the probability of an action may move away from the policy that collected the batch. Past that limit, the change earns nothing more in the objective.
Running a policy so that each action changes what the policy sees next.
Scoring a policy by letting it drive, on the real arm, in a simulator or in a world model, and counting the successes. Each of its actions changes what it sees next.
An EC2 setting that packs instances close together on the network. AWS Batch requires one for EFA jobs.
The one task governance object per cluster that holds priority classes and how idle compute is shared.
The Kueue object that holds a quota per flavor for the whole cluster.
The plugin standard that Kubernetes pod networks are built on. The Amazon VPC CNI used in the cloud is not compatible with hybrid nodes.
In PolaRiS, a short fine-tuning of a policy on simulated demonstrations from other scanned scenes. It gets the policy used to how the simulator renders images.
A method for compressing video into a file and turning the file back into frames. The encoder does the compressing, and the decoder turns the file back into frames.
A language model that works through an agent program, which lets it read and write files and run commands. In section 19, the coding agent's task is to improve a robot's policy.
A group of ClusterQueues that lend each other unused quota.
A shortcut in which the encoder maps every input to the same latent. The loss drops to zero and the latents become useless.
The search, repeated in every physics step, for the shapes in the scene that touch. MuJoCo runs it in three phases: a broad, a mid and a near phase.
The unit of software that Greengrass runs. A component is a recipe plus its artifacts.
The disk area where the nucleus keeps component artifacts. Its limit is 10 GB by default.
The way small mistakes grow over a task. A small mistake moves the robot into a situation that the demonstrations never showed, the policy makes a larger mistake there, and the error keeps growing.
A team's quota: resources, a sharing strategy, a borrow limit and a preemption rule.
A major.minor version number that names a GPU generation. An engine records it, and TensorRT checks it when the engine loads.
The pool of capacity behind a Batch queue: a type, a list of instance types, an allocation strategy and a vCPU floor and ceiling.
A machine that runs jobs. In PCS, each compute node is one EC2 instance that runs slurmd and the PCS agent.
The PCS object that describes how nodes are created: the instance types, the minimum and maximum instance count, the subnets, the image and one purchase option.
The range of true success rates that could plausibly have produced an observed count. At the 95% level, the range contains the true rate about nineteen times in twenty.
The NodePool setting for how long Karpenter waits before removing a node it no longer needs.
Karpenter removing or replacing nodes to cut cost.
A rule that the next state must obey, for example that two touching shapes do not pass through each other.
A table with one row per constraint that says how far each joint's motion moves that constraint. Its transpose turns constraint forces into joint forces.
The iterative search, inside every physics step, for the constraint forces that keep all constraints true at once.
A counted resource in AWS Batch, such as a licence token, that a job waits for until it is free. You can model one robot station as a consumable resource with a count of one.
A place where two simulated shapes touch, such as a finger on the cube.
The copy of the encoder that sees only the visible tokens. The loss trains it.
HyperPod's default way of filling groups: it records a target count, retries failed launches in the background and lets jobs start on the capacity that has arrived.
Latents of different inputs that a contrastive loss term pushes apart to prevent collapse. Contrastive learning is an older method than variance and covariance terms.

The stack of control loops on a robot. Each loop runs more slowly and makes bigger decisions than the loop below it. On the SO-101, the loops are the servo loop, the host loop, the policy and the planner.
The length of one tick. It is 33.3 ms at 30 Hz.
The number of ticks per second. It is 30 Hz, or 33.3 ms per tick, when LeRobot records.
One decision by the policy and the motion that follows it. In the SO-101 vision task, one control step covers 20 physics steps.
A version of an episode reduced to its geometry, such as edges, depth or a segmentation map. A video generator uses it to keep the new video's geometry the same.
A faster, simpler loop that follows the targets that a planner or a policy gives it.
The share of back-end bound slots in which the execution units are busy or operations wait on each other's results. A faster core helps such a job, and faster memory does not.
A device that runs the Greengrass software.
A comparison of two vectors that is 1 when they point in the same direction. The compiled model's outputs are expected to reach 0.999 or higher against the original's.
NVIDIA's current family of video world models, released at the end of May 2026 in three sizes: Super, Nano and Edge.
NVIDIA's toolkit for curating physical AI training data. It runs as a pipeline of CPU and GPU stages on a cluster.
Whether the parts of a job exchange data with each other while they run.
Whether two dimensions rise and fall together across a batch. It is 0 when they carry unrelated information.
The part of a CPU core that executes the decoded instructions on its arithmetic units.
The part of a CPU core that fetches instructions and decodes them.
The encoder's quality setting: a single number for how much detail the encoder may discard. A lower value gives better quality and larger files.
The plug-in form in which Kubernetes mounts storage into pods as volumes.
NVIDIA's programming layer for running code on its GPUs.
A sequence of GPU kernel launches that is recorded once and then started again with one call.
Choosing which recordings a model learns from, for example by dropping failed attempts, clips where nothing moves and near copies.
A model trained to rebuild its input through a small random vector. ACT uses one during training to keep different ways of doing a task apart.
A Kubernetes object that runs one pod on every matching node.

A method from 2011 that runs the learned policy, asks the expert to label the situations it reaches, adds them to the data and retrains. It needs an expert who can be asked for the right action in the situations that the policy reaches.
How hard a servo or a joint brakes per unit of speed.
A way to train on several GPUs. Each GPU keeps a copy of the model and works through its own share of the batch, and the GPUs combine their gradients into one update per step.
The component of a training job that prepares samples. Here it extracts frames from the video and varies them, on the CPU cores of the training instance.
A CPU process that reads and decodes samples and prepares them into batches for the GPU.
NVIDIA's tool for monitoring a fleet of GPUs. It reports separate fields for each GPU resource, such as SM activity, tensor activity and memory activity.
A transform that rewrites a signal as a sum of cosine waves, so a smooth motion needs only a few numbers.
AWS's term for environments whose network link is unreliable.
A sampling method for diffusion models that skips iterations, so fewer network passes are needed at inference.
To turn compressed video back into frames of pixels. Training repeats this work every time it reads a frame.
A network that redraws the pixels from an encoder's output.
The share of time that a GPU's video decoder was in use. nvidia-smi reports it separately from the utilisation of the GPU's compute part.
The curation step that removes near copies. It clusters the clip embeddings and drops clips that are too close to another clip, so that near-identical recordings do not outweigh the rest.
An optional stress test HyperPod runs on a new or replaced instance before work lands on it.
An action given as an offset from the previous action. Because each action builds on the one before it, errors add up along the sequence.
A recording of a person doing the task through the robot. It stores the observations and the six target angles that the person's hand asked for.
One round in which the network predicts the noise in the current chunk and part of that noise is subtracted.
One run of a generator's transformer over all its tokens, which removes a little of the noise. A video generator makes tens of these passes per clip. Section 4 explains diffusion and flow matching.
One network pass that moves a noisy chunk closer to a finished one. Configuration files use the name for both diffusion iterations and flow-matching steps.
A neural-network layer that multiplies its input by a weight matrix, so every output depends on every input. The policy test program is six of them, run on one CPU core.
The full list of components that a thing or a thing group should run. A deployment stays in place, so a device that reconnects later still receives it.
A DaemonSet that advertises a node's devices to Kubernetes; the NVIDIA one advertises GPUs as nvidia.com/gpu.
NVIDIA's desk-side Arm computer. It has a GPU and 128 GB of memory that the CPU and the GPU share.
A second inference library for generative models. NVIDIA benchmarks it alongside its PyTorch scripts.
A policy that starts from a chunk of random noise and removes predicted noise over many iterations until an action chunk remains.
A hash of a file's or an image's content, computed in advance. A reference by digest names exactly one set of bytes, and a mismatch makes the deployment fail.
A partial collapse in which the latents still differ but all lie inside a thin slice of the space, so most of their numbers carry no information.
A latent world model built on a frozen pretrained image encoder.
AWS Direct Connect, a private network link to AWS. It is one of the ways an EKS hybrid node can reach its cluster's VPC.
Direct lighting is light that reaches a surface straight from a lamp, without bouncing off other surfaces. Isaac Lab's Newton Warp renderer computes only direct lighting.
A MuJoCo integrator that its documentation recommends when stiff springs, position servos or strong damping interact with contacts.
A transformer used to refine noise into an output, which in a VLA is an action chunk.
The AWS-provided Greengrass component that pulls container images, including images from private Amazon ECR repositories.
One independent way in which a mechanism can move. Each rotating joint of the arm adds one.
Changing the simulated arm and scene at the start of every episode, so that the real arm falls inside the range of conditions the policy trained on.
The Kubernetes API in which a driver publishes devices with attributes and a pod claims one by description.
The state Batch puts an instance in on the Spot notice: running jobs continue and no new job is placed on it.
A recipe in which a fine-tuned video model invents robot episodes and a second model recovers their actions.
NVIDIA's world-action model from February 2026. Its paper gave the name world-action model to this design.
A 2024 method in which a language model writes the reward and proposes the domain-randomisation ranges.
A node no longer matching its NodePool or image, which makes Karpenter replace it.
The robot platform that RoboArena's evaluators share, so that every lab runs the policies on the same model of robot.
How long one unit of a job's work runs.
The network disk of an EC2 instance. The instance type sets its maximum throughput.
The AWS service that rents virtual machines, called instances.
The EC2 API that fills one capacity request from a list of instance types.
The Karpenter object holding the AWS settings for nodes: image, role, subnets, security groups, disks, reservations.
AWS's store for container images.
The AWS service that starts containers on instances; a Batch compute environment contains an ECS cluster that its instances join.

A computer that sits next to the robot instead of in the cloud. You buy it once instead of renting it by the hour, so you compare edge computers on the work they do per unit of energy and on their purchase price.
The EC2 network device for traffic between instances. It bypasses the operating system kernel so that many machines can train as one. The small GPU instance sizes do not have it.
A shared network file system on AWS that a Batch job can mount as a volume, for example to keep checkpoints.
The interface MuJoCo uses for hardware-accelerated rendering without a display.
Video shot from the point of view of the person doing the task.
AWS's managed Kubernetes service.
The managed form of Karpenter-based scaling, in which AWS also runs the node software.

expansion: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service Hybrid Nodes
meaning: A feature that joins a machine on your own premises to a Kubernetes cluster in the cloud as a worker node.
A HyperPod feature that grows and shrinks a training job by checkpointing and resuming with a different number of workers.
The candidates with the lowest cost in one CEM round. CEM refits its sampling distribution to them.
A running average in which recent values count most and older values fade out. The target encoder's weights are an EMA of the context encoder's weights.
A vector, a list of numbers that a model computes for a clip. Clips with similar content get vectors that are close together.
A robot body, with its joints, sensors and action space.
The EC2 network device that moves data over ordinary IP networking.
A sensor on a joint that reports the joint's angle as a whole number of steps. On the SO-101, a full turn is 4096 steps.

The program or circuit that compresses video at recording time. The word has this meaning from section 9, Collecting Data, to the end of section 11, Augmentation and Synthetic Data. In section 3, The Robot as a Computer, encoder meant the angle sensor on a joint.
The tool at the end of the arm. On the SO-101, it is the gripper.
An action that gives the pose of the gripper. Before an arm can follow it, inverse kinematics must convert it into joint angles (section 3, The Robot as a Computer).
A way of stating an action as the position and orientation of the gripper. Software then converts it into joint angles.
The distance between a predicted latent and a target latent or a goal latent. It is low when the two are a plausible match.
The file that TensorRT writes. It holds a model compiled for the GPU type and the TensorRT version it was built with, and it fails to deserialize anywhere else.
A 2026 research system from NVIDIA and two universities. It gives each of eight real robot stations its own coding agent, and each agent improves the policy against a frozen success check.
One simulated copy of the scene, such as an arm, a table and a cube. A GPU advances thousands of environments in one batch.
One attempt at the task, recorded or simulated. A recorded episode is a table of joint readings and motor commands over time, plus one video per camera.
One pass of training over every frame of the dataset.
In the compounding-error bound, the probability that the policy disagrees with the expert on one decision, measured on situations that the expert visited.
A short straight step along the current velocity, after which the network is asked for the velocity again.
The name under which Linux exposes the PMU of one core type, such as armv8_pmuv3_1 for the Cortex-X925 on a DGX Spark. You name perf events through it.
One teleoperated recording made so that every fitted constant acts in the data. On every joint it includes small corrections, fast motion, starts and stops, and moves from rest.

LeRobot's RTC setting for how many actions of the old chunk the new chunk stays consistent with, which covers the frozen and guided zones together. The default is 10, typical values are 8 to 12, and it must be at least inference_delay.
The person (or controller) whose demonstrations the policy is trained to copy.
The bits of a floating-point number that set how large or small it can get.
A countable thing beyond CPU and memory that a node advertises and a pod claims in whole units, such as nvidia.com/gpu.
An AWS Batch policy that divides a shared queue among teams or agents by weight. It divides capacity in proportion and does not set a GPU-hour budget.
An action tokeniser that compresses a chunk with a cosine transform and byte-pair encoding before the language model predicts it.
A feature is a label on a group's nodes, and a constraint is the job option that asks for nodes with that label. A job uses them to choose a group when several groups serve one queue.
The default order of a Batch queue: the job at the front goes next, and blocks the rest if it cannot be placed.
The dataset call that closes the Parquet writers. If a script does not call it, the Parquet files are corrupt.
Training a pretrained model further on new data, such as recorded episodes of one task.
A test of whether two success counts could come from the same true rate. It counts how often luck alone would split the pooled failures at least as unevenly as the observed split.
An AWS IoT feature that makes the device registry and the shadows searchable. With it, one query can find, for example, the arms on a new policy whose reported success rate fell.
A way to onboard many devices. Each device ships with the same shared claim certificate, and it exchanges that certificate for its own on its first connection.
An instance group that lists up to 20 instance types in priority order and falls back down the list when capacity is missing.
A method that turns noise into a sample. A network is trained to output the direction from noise to data, and sampling follows that direction in a few steps.
Progress through the sampling, from 0 (pure noise) to 1 (finished chunk). All of it passes inside one policy call, so it is separate from the robot's clock.
Throwing away the micro-operations started after a wrong branch guess, and restarting from the right place.
Arm's per-core adjustment that moves the slots lost while recovering from a flush out of front-end bound and into bad speculation.
The arm that receives the leader arm's joint angles as targets and does the task. It is the robot used throughout this dive.
A sixteen-bit format with a five-bit exponent. It overflows in pi0.5's attention layers.
Single-precision floating point, the full-precision format. GR00T N1.7's vision encoder stays at FP32.
A four-bit format with two exponent bits and one mantissa bit. NVFP4 adds a scale factor per block.
An 8-bit number format that takes 1 byte per weight.
The number of video frames in one second of video.
The limit on dry friction inside a joint. MuJoCo treats it as a constraint, and the SO-101 scene sets it on every joint.
The time at which an episode begins inside a camera's shared MP4 file. The reader adds it to a row's timestamp to find that row's frame.
The stages of a core's pipeline that predict which instructions come next, fetch them and decode them into micro-operations.
The share of slots left empty because the front end had no micro-operation ready.
Describes weights that a fine-tune does not update. Frozen weights need no gradient and no optimiser state in GPU memory.
A fine-tuning setting that leaves the vision-language model unchanged and trains only the action head and the layer that feeds it.
A pretrained encoder whose weights stay fixed while a predictor is trained on top of it.

The three parts of a new chunk under real-time chunking. Frozen actions were already played from the old chunk, guided actions are pulled toward the old chunk with a decaying weight, and free actions lie beyond the old chunk's end.

A form of data-parallel training that splits the weights, gradients and optimiser state across the GPUs instead of keeping a full copy on each. You use it when the training state of a model does not fit on one GPU.
AWS's managed Lustre file system, which many processes can read in parallel. It is used to keep data and checkpoints between training jobs.
A transformer layer in which every position on the grid is compared with every other position, so its work grows faster than the number of positions.
Further training that updates every weight of a pretrained model.
One instruction that computes a x b + c. A loop of independent scalar fused multiply-adds measures a core's multiply-add throughput without its vector units.
G and P are EC2 GPU instance families. G instances have GPUs with RT cores, and P instances have data-centre training GPUs.
EC2 GPU instances whose GPUs also have graphics and video hardware, including RT cores.
A tuning number in a controller. It sets how strongly the controller reacts to the error.
How hard a servo pushes per unit of position error. The model file calls it stiffness.
Scheduling all of a job's pods together or none of them.

A fitting method for sums of squared misses. At each step it works out how each miss changes with each parameter, and then moves all the parameters at once to where the squared misses would be smallest.
A method that represents a filmed place as a cloud of small, soft, coloured blobs. The blobs are adjusted until pictures drawn from the cloud match the video frames.
The units that make up most of a GPU and can run any arithmetic in parallel. They are separate from the tensor cores, the ray-tracing cores and the video engines.

The general compute cores are the units of a GPU that run ordinary GPU code. They run batched physics, ray tracers written as GPU code, the parts of a neural network other than its matrix multiplications, and the lighting and shading of an RTX renderer.
A GPU's ordinary arithmetic units, as opposed to its tensor cores or its ray-tracing cores.
An action head that draws one sample from the set of good answers. A regression head, by contrast, returns a single averaged answer.
The binary gigabyte, which is slightly larger than a GB.
A picture of the desired end state. The planner tries to reach the latent of this picture.
The spacing of keyframes in a video. A GOP size of 2 means a keyframe every second frame, which makes reading a random frame cheap.
NVIDIA's package that installs the driver, toolkit, device plugin, node labelling and monitoring together.
In nvidia-smi, the percentage of the sample period during which at least one kernel was executing on the GPU.
The share of time during which at least one program (kernel) was running on the GPU. It does not show how much of the GPU's capacity was in use.
Fixed-function circuits on a GPU that only compress and decompress video. They are separate from the tensor cores that run neural networks.
One GPU running for one hour.
The number of GPUs a job uses multiplied by the hours it uses them. It measures GPU time, not work, because GPU models differ in speed.
NVIDIA's world-action model, described in a November 2026 whitepaper. NVIDIA announced its code for December 2026, and as of November 2026 the code cannot be downloaded yet.
A large robot model from NVIDIA. This section uses it as the example of a large policy.
For each weight that trains, the direction in which a training step moves it. It takes GPU memory alongside the weight.
A training setting that recomputes the activations during the backward pass instead of storing them. It trades extra compute for less GPU memory.
A planning method that computes, through the predictor, which way to change the candidate actions. A search only samples them.
The corrections to a model's weights that a training step computes. In multi-node training, every node exchanges them with the others at every step.
The Arm processors that AWS designs for EC2. Graviton2, 3, 4 and 5 use the Neoverse N1, V1, V2 and V3 cores.
How Slurm counts resources that are neither CPU cores nor memory. GPUs are the main example.
An RL algorithm that scores each attempt against the other attempts collected with it.
LeRobot's default RTC mode. It applies guidance at run time and works with ordinary flow-matching checkpoints.
Another video compression standard. LeRobot can write it in software or through hardware encoders.
LeRobot's tuning rule written as a formula: with asynchronous inference, one call may take at most half the time its chunk lasts, L <= H Δt / 2.
A gripper with a camera mounted on it, which a person holds to do the task without a robot. Software reconstructs the gripper's path afterwards.
A TensorRT build option that makes an engine loadable on other GPU types. In TensorRT 11.5.0 it exists on Arm server-class Linux and not on JetPack.
A fixed circuit in a GPU or processor that compresses video without loading the CPU cores.
Counters built into a processor that record events such as clock cycles spent waiting for memory. They show which resource held a program back.
Running a simulator with no window and no camera images.
The HyperPod process on each node that watches for hardware faults and labels the node's health.
A Kubernetes package; HyperPod's chart installs its health agent, device plug-ins and training operators on the EKS cluster.
A third video compression standard, also called H.265. LeRobot can write it through hardware encoders.
RL run directly on a real arm. It starts from a few demonstrations, and a person takes over to correct attempts that are going wrong.
The number of actions ahead that each candidate looks during planning.
The number of decisions that a policy takes in one task.
The laptop or small single-board computer that the arm and the cameras connect to by USB. It runs the control loop.
Large simulation and scientific jobs that run across many servers, which exchange data while they compute. AWS's HPC team tested such a job on Spot Instances.
The site where LeRobot datasets and models are published.

A way of recording in which a trained policy drives the arm and a person takes over before it fails, so that the person's recovery becomes training data. LeRobot describes it in its guide to human-in-the-loop data collection.
A robot with two legs and two arms.
A machine outside AWS, such as a lab workstation, joined to an EKS cluster as a node.
The object that lists which instance groups Karpenter may raise.
The HyperPod training operator's job object, whose runPolicy carries retry counts and rules that detect a hung job.
Times per second.
The AWS service that defines roles and what each role is allowed to call.

expansion: International Conference on Robotics and Automation
meaning: A robotics research conference. The REAL-I robot challenge was held there in 2026.
A small random change to a camera frame at training time, such as a change in brightness or a slight rotation. The recorded actions stay unchanged.
A public set of labelled photos. ACT's ResNet-18 image backbone starts from weights trained on it.
The NVIDIA service that lets GPUs in different nodes share memory. On PCS, each job needs an IMEX domain of its own.
MuJoCo's recommended integrator. It rescales the acceleration using how speed-dependent forces, such as damping, change with speed.
Two kinds of test. In distribution, the object starts in positions that the demonstrations covered. Out of distribution, it starts somewhere new.

A workload type. The work splits into many short pieces that do not depend on each other, so a lost machine costs only the piece it was running. These jobs fit a queue that retries failed pieces, on Spot Instances.
The table that plays the role of mass for a jointed body. It includes how accelerating one joint loads the others.
In the real-time chunking paper, d = floor(L / Δt): the length of one call counted in whole control periods, rounded down. LeRobot passes it as inference_delay.
LeRobot's RTC argument for the call's latency in control steps. LeRobot passes it with every call, because the latency varies at run time.
The image-editing task of filling a missing region so that it matches its surroundings. Real-time chunking treats the start of a new chunk the same way.
HyperPod's unit of capacity: a named set of instances of one type (or a flexible list of types) with a count and one capacity market.
The sentence that tells a VLA which task to do. The model receives it on every call.
The number of finished instructions divided by the number of clock cycles. It shows how much work a core did per cycle, but not why the rest of its capacity went unused.
The last part of a physics step. It uses the accelerations to advance the speeds, and the speeds to advance the positions, by one timestep.
Whether a job can stop and restart without losing more than one unit of work.
The Amazon SQS queue through which Karpenter receives EC2 events such as the Spot interruption warning.
A person taking over the arm for a moment during an autonomous attempt. The person's action replaces the policy's action and is stored with the rest of the data.
A network that works out which actions would produce a given piece of video.
The calculation of the joint angles that put the gripper at a given position and orientation.
A network that looks at two frames and outputs the action that happened between them.
Devices outside the data centre that connect to a cloud service. Here, the device is the robot computer.
The local socket through which a component talks to the nucleus, for example to defer an update. Each operation must be granted in an accessControl policy.
NVIDIA's framework for robot learning. It runs on Isaac Sim, and since version 3.0 it can also run without it.
The replay tool in Isaac Lab. It cuts demonstrations into subtasks, fits them to a new scene, replays them and keeps the ones that succeed.
NVIDIA's evaluation tool for its Isaac Lab simulator. It can run perturbation sweeps over lighting, backgrounds, camera parameters and object mass.
NVIDIA's simulator application. It draws simulated cameras with a ray tracer that needs RT cores.
A bell-shaped cloud with the same spread in every direction and no correlation between dimensions.
Google's array library for Python. MJX-JAX is written in it.
A model design that predicts a compact summary of the scene instead of its pixels.
The name that a peer-reviewed 2026 study gives to world models trained only by a predictive loss in latent space. The study compares their planners.
NVIDIA's software bundle for Jetson devices, with Linux, GPU drivers and libraries.
NVIDIA's line of onboard computers for robots. The Jetson AGX Thor and the Jetson Orin are two of them.
NVIDIA's small robot computer. It is the other machine we measured.
An NVIDIA onboard computer for robots. The GR00T N1.7 model card calls it Jetson AGX Thor.
An AWS IoT remote operation that is sent to many devices. Greengrass sends a group deployment as a job, and the job sets the rollout rate, the abort rule and the timeout.
One Slurm submission that expands into many numbered copies of the same script. Slurm schedules each copy as its own job.
The template of a Batch job: image, command, resource needs, retry strategy and timeout.
The run of an AWS IoT job on one device. An abort cancels only the executions that are still QUEUED, never those that are IN_PROGRESS.
The Batch object where jobs wait, with a priority and an ordered list of up to three compute environments.
Where a Batch job is: SUBMITTED, PENDING, RUNNABLE, STARTING, RUNNING, then SUCCEEDED or FAILED.
A Kubernetes object that manages several Jobs as one unit and restarts them together.
A way of stating an action as one target angle per motor.
An offset that the task adds to the simulated joint readings in each episode, to stand in for calibration error.
A clustering algorithm that groups vectors around a chosen number of centres.
An open-source Kubernetes scheduler with queues and quotas for GPU work.

The node autoscaler that launches a Kubernetes cluster's nodes on EKS. A NodePool's spec.limits can cap the number of GPUs directly, but Karpenter's limit check is only eventually consistent, so a fast burst of jobs can go over the limit.
A function that runs on the GPU. GPU utilisation in nvidia-smi counts the time during which at least one kernel is executing.
A program that runs on the GPU.
A video frame that is stored whole and can be decoded on its own. The other frames are stored as differences from the frames before them.
A file that describes the arm's link lengths and joint axes. Software needs it to convert between gripper poses and joint angles.
A number for how far one probability distribution is from another. It is zero when they match.
The Kubernetes controller that turns a training job description such as a PyTorchJob into pods.
A Kubernetes add-on that holds jobs against per-team quotas and decides when each is admitted.
A distance between two lists of numbers. You subtract them entry by entry, drop the signs and add up the results, or take their mean.
A loss that adds up the absolute differences between predicted and recorded values. LeRobot's code takes their mean instead of their sum.
The time one call takes. The computer next to the arm is sized by latency, because the arm has a fixed control period.
Latency is the time one step takes, which CPU MuJoCo minimises. Throughput is the total number of steps per unit of time, which MuJoCo Warp maximises.
The time from the capture of a camera frame to the moment the action computed from it reaches the servos, split into the waits that add up to it.

The internal code that an encoder makes of a frame or a clip: a grid or a vector of numbers. Both families of world model use one. In the pixel family, the latent is built to be decoded back into pixels.
World models that predict the encoder's summary of the next frames. They never draw a picture.
The second kind of model that the DreamGen paper names for recovering actions from generated video.
An EC2 object that holds the instance settings a compute node group cannot express itself, such as EFA interfaces, the placement group, capacity reservations and user data.
The second arm that a person moves by hand to demonstrate a task. The robot arm copies its movements while the demonstration is recorded. It is also called the teacher arm.
The program that stores transitions, does the gradient updates on a GPU and sends new weights to the actor.
An open-source library for recording robot data and training robot models. The arm in this dive follows its default settings.
The file layout that LeRobot v0.7.0 writes. It stores table rows in Parquet files, camera frames in MP4 files and a set of metadata files, and each file holds many episodes.
LeRobot's evaluation tool. It runs a checkpoint in closed loop in a batch of simulated environments and reports the success rate with a 95% Wilson interval.
The second level of top-down analysis, which splits back-end bound into memory bound and core bound. Arm's files for the Neoverse V3, Cortex-X925 and Cortex-A725 define it with events of their own.
A small latent world model of about 15M parameters that keeps one vector per frame.
A JEPA world model of about 15M parameters. It trains the encoder and the predictor together and prevents collapse with SIGReg.
A suite of simulated manipulation tasks used as a benchmark.
A laser scanner that measures the distance to surrounding surfaces.
The part of a recipe that holds the commands to install, start and stop a component.
A set-up script HyperPod runs once on each new node.

The three conditions under which a ratio of two rates describes the two machines: the same unit, the same model and the same software release. For a vendor's figure, the runtime and the power mode must match too.

A LeRobot mode that runs the policy in a background thread of the process that drives the arm. If the arm runs out of actions, a supported robot holds its last commanded position for up to one second by default, and then the run stops with a fault.
Kueue's per-namespace queue, the one a team's jobs name in their label.
The always-on machine where users type Slurm commands. In PCS, it is a static compute node group that is attached to no queue.
A workload type. One job keeps one machine busy for hours, and a lost machine costs the work done since the last checkpoint.
One of the six steps that the arm's data passes through: collect, curate, simulate, train, evaluate and deploy.
A fine-tune that adds small matrices to the model and trains only those, leaving the original weights frozen.

One of the separate resources inside a computer that a workload can run out of, such as the front end or back end of a CPU core, memory bandwidth, a GPU engine, storage or the network. When one resource is fully used, the others sit partly idle.
The SageMaker Training Jobs setting that runs a job on Spot Instances. It copies the job's checkpoints to S3 and back, and resumes the job after an interruption. It does not fall back to On-Demand.
A HyperPod feature for PyTorch on EKS. It keeps checkpoints in the nodes' CPU memory, copies them to adjacent nodes, and periodically saves them to durable storage such as S3.
The bits of a floating-point number that set how precisely it is stored.
A learned placeholder vector, tagged with a position, that tells the predictor to output the latent that belongs at that position.
Removing some tokens before the encoder sees them, so that the model has to predict the latents of what was hidden.
LeRobot's RTC limit on how strongly the new chunk is pulled toward the old one. The default is 10.0.
The largest number of vCPUs that an AWS Batch compute environment may run at once. It limits GPUs only through the instance types that the environment is allowed to launch.
The middle value of a set of timed calls. It describes the typical call, not the slowest one.
The rate at which memory delivers data to the processor, measured in GB/s.

The share of back-end bound slots in which the core waits for data to be loaded or stored. Faster memory helps such a job: more bandwidth if its loads stream through memory, and lower latency if each load waits for the one before.
The time one fetch from memory takes, measured in nanoseconds. It becomes the limit when each address depends on the value fetched before it.
The share of cycles in which the back end waited on memory, counted by a separate event.
A mesh is a surface stored as a set of triangles. A simulator stores every shape it draws as a mesh.
The files that describe a dataset's schema and record where each episode sits inside the shared data and video files.
An EC2 instance with no virtual machine layer between the operating system and the hardware.
One of the smaller internal steps that a core splits each program instruction into. Intel writes it as uOp.
A small loop built to exercise one resource of a core, such as its multiply-add units or its memory.
A lightweight virtual machine. Nitro Sandboxes use the Firecracker microVM.
NVIDIA's way of dividing one GPU into isolated slices. On a GPU split this way, nvidia-smi cannot report decoder or GPU utilisation.
The system, published in 2023, that introduced replaying a few human demonstrations in simulation from new object positions.
The floor a compute environment keeps running, the current target that Batch moves with queue demand, and the ceiling it may reach.
MuJoCo's step function. It runs 26 stages in four groups: position, velocity, force and acceleration, and the integrator.
MuJoCo's JAX interface. It runs on two engines: MJX-JAX, a rewrite of MuJoCo in JAX, and MJX-Warp, which calls MuJoCo Warp.
An experiment tracking server and model registry, offered managed by SageMaker.
A plain stack of fully connected layers.
One separate group of valid answers. A task that can be done in two distinct ways has two modes.
A text file of typed-in values that describes every link, joint, servo and shape in a scene.
The fraction of its old value that a target weight keeps at each EMA update. V-JEPA 2 uses 0.99925.
A client that presents an S3 bucket as a local file system for reading and creating files.

term: Mountpoint for Amazon S3 CSI driver
meaning: The driver that presents an S3 bucket as a volume in a pod.
A control method in which you plan a sequence of actions through a model, execute only the first part, observe the result, and plan again.
An NVIDIA feature that runs several processes on one GPU at the same moment.
A lightweight protocol in which a device publishes small messages to named topics, and subscribers receive them.
The average of the squared differences between two sets of numbers.
The physics simulator covered in section 12, Physics Simulation. The episode frames and the clip in this section are rendered from a simulated SO-101 in MuJoCo.
Google DeepMind's library of robot model files for MuJoCo, which includes a model of the SO-101.
Google DeepMind's suite of ready-made robot tasks and training code. It includes the SO-101 pick-cube task.
A version of MuJoCo written in NVIDIA's Warp framework. It steps many worlds in one batch on an NVIDIA GPU.
The system-identification toolbox that ships with MuJoCo 4.0. The SO-101 script built on it fits 24 servo parameters from one episode.
One Batch job that spans several instances, with a main node that starts first; On-Demand only.
A workload type. One run spreads across many machines that exchange data at every training step, so losing one machine loses the current step on all of them. Spot Instances are not an option.
Describes demonstrations whose good answers form several separate groups. This meaning is separate from multimodal models, which take both images and text.
A way to send one S3 object as many parts, so that a dropped connection costs only one part.

What perf does when it cannot count every requested event at the same time. The events take turns, perf scales each count up to the whole run, and it reports the share of the measurement time during which each counter was running.
NVIDIA's training framework. HyperPod's checkpointless training is built on it.
Arm's vector instructions, which work on several numbers at once.
A GPU physics engine built on Warp. It offers several solvers, and MuJoCo Warp is one of them.
The lightweight ray tracer in the base install of Isaac Lab 3.0. It draws direct lighting only and runs without Isaac Sim.
The packaged container that NVIDIA ships for serving a model. Its support matrix prints the minimum GPU memory per device.
An AWS feature, announced on 9 November 2026, that runs a pod, task or workload in its own Firecracker microVM with its own kernel. It runs CPU work only, with no GPU passthrough.
One server in a training job, such as an EC2 instance with eight GPUs.
A script that PCS runs on a node at one of two boot stages: nodeBootstrapped, before slurmd starts, or nodeReady, after it starts.
The layer that starts a machine when a job is waiting and removes it when nothing is.
The cluster setting that lets HyperPod reboot or replace a faulty node without being asked.
Karpenter's record of one instance on its way to being a node: Launched, Registered, Initialized.
A Karpenter object that describes which nodes may be launched and, through spec.limits, how many resources they may use in total.
The rate the recorder was asked to run at, 30 fps by default. The recorder computes every timestamp from this rate, whatever rate the recording loop actually achieved.
NVIDIA's profiler for a single GPU kernel. It reports the kernel's throughput against the GPU's maximum and draws a roofline chart.
NVIDIA's profiler that puts the CPU samples, GPU calls and kernels of one application on a single timeline.
The Greengrass program installed on the device. It installs, starts and watches components.
The smaller Greengrass nucleus, written in C. It has fewer features than the Java nucleus.
The fixed-function circuit on an NVIDIA GPU that decompresses video.
The fixed-function circuit on an NVIDIA GPU that compresses video.
The name NVIDIA gives to the number format of its quantised GR00T N1.7 build.
NVIDIA's command-line tool that reports GPU status, including utilisation and the power of the GPU.
The percent of time in the sample period during which at least one kernel was running on the GPU. It says nothing about how much of the GPU the kernel used.
NVIDIA's direct connection between GPUs.
The input to a policy at one instant. On the SO-101, it is the six joint angles and one image from each camera.
Capacity held for a named instance type in one Availability Zone for any duration, charged at the On-Demand rate.
A purchase option in which you pay for the instance while it runs, with no commitment, and AWS does not take it back.
An On-Demand Capacity Reservation is an EC2 reservation type that covers G instances, which Capacity Blocks do not.
The small computer next to the arm that reads the cameras and joints, runs the policy and sends targets to the motors.
A portable file format for a model graph. It is used to hand a trained checkpoint over to the device.
Two Arm events. OP_SPEC counts the micro-operations dispatched through a slot, including those later thrown away, and OP_RETIRED counts the micro-operations that retired.
Another robot project. The SO-101 maker's model file adapts its motor parameters from it.
Scoring a policy on recorded frames by comparing the action it predicts with the recorded action. The policy's own actions never change what it sees next.
Physical Intelligence's open repository. It holds pi0, pi0-FAST and pi0.5.
The geometry type that Isaac Sim's scene files use to store Gaussian splats.
A 7B robot model whose head was changed from writing one token at a time to one parallel pass that regresses the whole chunk.
The running statistics that the optimiser keeps from step to step for each weight that trains. A frozen weight has no optimiser state.
OptiX is NVIDIA's ray-tracing library for RTX GPUs. MuJoCo Warp's optional hardware back end is built on it, and MuJoCo Warp falls back to the Warp back end when OptiX is unavailable.
A service that queues jobs and starts machines for them, such as AWS Batch, AWS Parallel Computing Service, Amazon SageMaker HyperPod or Amazon EKS.
NVIDIA's open-source workflow orchestrator for physical AI pipelines on Kubernetes clusters.
Conditions that the training demonstrations did not show, such as new objects, sizes or orientations.
OVRTX is the RTX renderer that Isaac Lab 3.0's documentation recommends. It runs without Isaac Sim and needs RT cores.
EC2 GPU instances built for training. Their GPUs do not have RT cores, and the H100 GPUs in P5 cannot decode AV1.
How often two equally good policies would show a gap at least as large as the one observed.
The time within which half of all calls finish. It describes the typical call.
The p50 is the median time per call. The p99 is the time that only one call in a hundred exceeds.
The time within which ninety-nine calls in a hundred finish. You compare it with the time that a chunk leaves for a call when one late call in a hundred is acceptable.
In LeRobot's cadence report, the time left in a tick after the loop's work. A value near zero leaves nothing to absorb a slow tick.
Independent copies of one simulated scene that a single GPU simulates at the same time.
A compressed table file format that stores data column by column. LeRobot stores the table rows, one for each time step, in Parquet files.
A named Slurm queue in front of a set of nodes. Each PCS queue is one partition.

The share of rollouts that contain a success within k attempts after one reset. pass@1 is the first-try rate. pass@8 counts first tries and retries together, and you cannot split it into the two without knowing the first-try rate.
One of the small squares that a camera image is cut into. Each patch becomes one token.
Managed Slurm: AWS runs the Slurm controller and compute node groups launch EC2 instances for waiting jobs.
A PID controller with the integral term switched off. It pushes in proportion to the error and brakes when the error shrinks fast.
The job states that squeue shows: PD while the job waits, CF while its nodes are being brought up, and R while it runs.
A measure from -1 to 1 of how closely two sets of scores rise and fall together.
The state of a pod that no node can hold yet; on a cluster that scales from zero it is the request for a machine.
The ratio of two rates that were each measured on one core. It stands for the ratio of the two machines only for a job that keeps one core busy.
The maximum number of contacts and constraints that each MuJoCo Warp world reserves up front, 64 and 256 in the pick-cube task. Memory and computation scale with these limits.

One call in a hundred is slower than the p99. So if you compare the p99 with the time that a chunk leaves for a call, you accept one late call in a hundred. If you accept none, compare the slowest call instead.
The Linux tool that reads the processor's counters. The perf stat command runs a program and prints the counter totals.
The Linux tool that reads the PMU counters over one run of a program.
Scoring the same checkpoint across controlled changes to one scene, such as lighting, backgrounds, camera parameters and object mass. You keep only the checkpoints whose success rate holds.
One real processor core. With two threads per core, 24 vCPUs are 12 physical cores.
A physics engine is the software that moves a simulated scene forward in time. PhysX, Newton and MuJoCo Warp are the physics engines in this section.
A program that holds a scene as numbers and computes how the scene moves, one small time step after another.
One call of the simulator's step function. It takes the state and the motor commands and returns the state one timestep later.
NVIDIA's physics engine. Isaac Sim uses it, and Isaac Lab can run on it.
A robot model from Physical Intelligence that produces action chunks by flow matching. Section 5, Vision-Language-Action Models, explains it in detail.
A later Physical Intelligence model that is pretrained with FAST tokens and then given a flow-matching action head for inference.
A controller that sets the motor drive from the error now (P), the sum of the error over time (I) and how fast the error is changing (D).
World models that predict the next camera frames. They predict a reconstruction code, which a decoder turns back into pixels.
In the figure of the two clocks, one backbone pass over the scene and the instruction.
A slower loop that decides what to do next and passes targets to a faster controller.
Choosing an action by trying many candidates in a world model, scoring each predicted future against a goal and running the best one.
The number of predictor steps that a planner looks ahead for each candidate.
A JEPA world model that trains its encoder with variance and covariance terms. The LeWorldModel authors count six tunable loss coefficients in it.
The set of event counters built into a processor.

The record of one workload on one machine. It gives the throughput, where the CPU's slots went, what lies behind the largest loss, the GPU readings when a GPU does the work, and how everything was counted.
The Kubernetes plugin that gives each pod an address. On an EKS hybrid node, you install and run it yourself, using Cilium or Calico.
A loop in which each read gives the address of the next read. It measures memory latency.
A research pipeline that builds scanned scenes from a short video and tests policies in them.
The trained model that controls the arm. It reads the camera images and the joint angles and decides how the motors move next.
One complete run of the policy model, from the prepared observation to a decoded chunk of actions.
One model family in LeRobot, which you select on the command line with --policy.type.
The program inside a servo that compares the measured angle with the goal angle and drives the motor to close the gap.
Any training that starts from a pretrained checkpoint. Its size ranges from one GPU to several servers.
The chance that a comparison detects a gap that is really there. At 80% power, the comparison detects the gap four times in five.
The power setting that a Jetson runs in. NVIDIA took its GR00T N1.7 figures in the MAXN mode, and our Jetson ran in the MAXN_SUPER mode. Record the mode with every figure.
An RL algorithm that alternates between collecting a batch of fresh attempts and making a limited update of the policy from that batch.

Of the attempts a check passes, the share that truly succeeded. It is the requirement that keeps false passes out of the grade, because an agent that optimises the grade can learn to chase them. Precision changes with the policy's true success rate. The share of failures that the check passes describes the check itself.
In a latent world model, the network that takes the current latent and an action and outputs the next latent in one pass.
One forward run of the predictor for one candidate and one step. A planner needs samples x iterations x horizon passes for each decision.
A scheduler stopping a running job to give its capacity to another; Batch does it only for SageMaker Training queues.
The sequence of image tokens and text tokens that enters the backbone on one call. The backbone reads it once, and its results are cached for the action head.
LeRobot's RTC setting for how the guidance weight decays. The code defaults to LINEAR, and the documentation recommends EXP.
The first training of a model, on data from many robots or on video, before the model has seen your robot.
The Spot allocation strategy that takes the lowest-priced pools among those with the most spare capacity.
Running several of a model's matrix multiplications as one GPU kernel. It is part of NVIDIA's optimised execution profile for GR00T N1.7 on Thor.
The robot's built-in safety halt.
Action labels that a second model infers from a generated video. The term comes from the DreamGen paper.
The purchase price of a board divided by the units of work per second that it sustains. It tells you what each unit per second of capacity cost to buy.
The way you pay for EC2 capacity. The four that matter here are On-Demand, Spot Instances, Capacity Blocks for ML and Savings Plans.
A simulated 2D pushing task used as a benchmark for small world models.
The Kubeflow Training Operator's object that describes one PyTorch training run.
MuJoCo's name for the vector of joint accelerations. It is the output of the force stages, before integration.
Storing a model's numbers in fewer bits, so that each layer moves less data from memory and does cheaper arithmetic.
Describes a model whose numbers are stored at lower precision, which makes it smaller and faster.
Storing a model's numbers in fewer bits. On the Jetson AGX Thor, NVIDIA's format for this is called mixed NVFP4.
The layer that holds waiting jobs and decides which runs next.
The PCS object that users submit jobs to. It is one Slurm partition, and it points at one or more compute node groups.
One supply line on a board. tegrastats reports the power of each rail, and on a Jetson the VDD_IN rail feeds the whole board.
Rasterisation makes an image by projecting each triangle onto it and filling the pixels that the triangle covers.
A framework that spreads Python jobs across the machines of a cluster.
A renderer that follows a ray from each pixel into the scene to find what it hits.
Ray tracing makes an image by following a ray from the camera through each pixel to the surface it hits, and then sending more rays from that point.
Separate GPU units that trace light rays to draw an image. The A100 and H100 do not have them.
RayCasterCamera is Isaac Lab's camera that casts its rays with Warp. The Isaac Lab paper found it faster than the tiled camera at low resolutions.
A robot challenge held at ICRA 2026. Its report names the closed-loop effects that open-loop error misses, and one of its teams used the validation action error to shortlist checkpoints.
A workload type. The job runs on the computer next to the arm and must never be interrupted, so no cloud scheduler is involved.
Bringing something real into the simulator. Examples are measured servo parameters, a scanned scene, or a policy trained on real data that is then tested in simulation.
An EC2 signal that a Spot instance is at elevated risk of interruption.
Of the attempts that truly succeeded, the share that a check passes.

expansion: RL with Experience and Corrections via Advantage-conditioned Policies
meaning: Physical Intelligence's method for improving a VLA from its own attempts and from human corrections.
A JSON or YAML file that defines a component's details, dependencies, artifacts and lifecycle commands.
A latent that has to keep enough information to rebuild every pixel. A video generator predicts this kind of latent.
LeRobot's setting for how much playback may remain in the action queue when the client asks for the next chunk.
The AWS location that an instance runs in. Prices differ between Regions.
A way of training in which the model learns by trial and reward.
An action given as an offset from the robot's state at the moment when the policy made its prediction.
The function that sets negative values to zero. It is applied after a layer of a neural network.
Running the policy on a server on another machine. The host next to the arm keeps the cameras and the motors.
The pipeline stage that separates a core's front end from its back end. Arm counts slots at this stage.
Drawing the image that a simulated camera would see.
Computing the image that a camera in the simulated scene would see.
A store of past transitions that training samples from again and again.
One running copy of a model, such as the captioning model in a curation pipeline.

A training failure in which an encoder gives every input the same vector. It can happen when the encoder's output is scored against other encodings, because identical vectors always agree. Section 7 covers how to prevent it.
Putting a job that lost its node back in the queue. The job then starts again from the first line of its script.
Putting the scene back to its starting state between attempts.
A standard image network. ACT in LeRobot uses it to turn each camera image into feature vectors.
Something a program can run out of, such as a core's arithmetic units, memory bandwidth or memory latency. The resource a program runs out of first is its bottleneck, and it sets the program's speed.
The Kueue object that describes one kind of node through node labels and tolerations.
The last pipeline stage. It makes the results of executed micro-operations final, in program order.
The share of slots that carried a micro-operation which finished and was kept. It measures the core's useful work.
The part of a job definition that says how many attempts a job gets and which failures are retried, for example only a status reason matching Host EC2*.
A number that scores an attempt or one step of an attempt. For example, the reward can be 1 when the block ends in the cup and 0 otherwise.
A way to train a policy from its own scored attempts at a task, so that it can become better than the demonstrations it started from.
A ranking of policies on real robots, built from blind pairwise comparisons run at seven academic institutions on the DROID platform. Simulators and world models are checked against it.
Meta's latent world model for robot arms. Its predictors have 22M to 8B parameters and work on a frozen 2B encoder.

The computer that runs the control loop and talks to the motors. On a finished robot it is usually a small board mounted on the robot, the onboard computer, but on a bench it can be a desktop connected to the arm.
The share of research wall-clock time during which the robot is running an experiment.
A run in which a trained policy controls the arm on its own.
In ENPIRE's headline score, one reset followed by up to eight attempts at the task. The scene is not reset between the attempts, and each retry follows the previous failure.
A loss term that runs the predictor on its own previous output and compares the result with the latent of the frame the robot actually reached.
A chart of a kernel's achieved speed against its arithmetic per byte of memory moved. The sloped part of the roof is the memory bandwidth limit, and the flat part is the peak compute limit.
In a LeRobot dataset, a row holds the joint positions and camera frames at one control tick of one episode. In the curation design note, a row is one entry of the recipe's input table.
Units in some NVIDIA GPUs that speed up the costliest step of ray tracing, which is finding which triangle a ray hits. The H100 and A100 do not have them.

A LeRobot mode that computes the next chunk while the arm plays the current one. Like LeRobot's asynchronous mode in its default configuration, it drops the actions in a new chunk whose ticks have already passed.
NVIDIA's ray-tracing renderer, used in Isaac Sim. It needs a GPU with RT cores.
RTX rendering is NVIDIA's name for rendering that hands the search for what each ray hits to the RT cores. Isaac Sim's renderer works this way.
In AWS IoT Core, a query over incoming messages. Its actions send the matching messages to other services, such as an S3 bucket.
The state of a job that is ready and waiting for capacity, including the whole time an instance is launching for it.
An RL method that trains from a replay buffer, so that each real step is reused in many updates.
The Slurm command that queries the accounting record of past jobs.
AWS's persistent training cluster. By default, it deploys a cluster in one Availability Zone.
A managed run of one training container that bills for the duration of the job and then shuts the instances down.
A SageMaker service that starts instances for one training job and shuts them down when the job ends.
A capacity reservation made through SageMaker for a HyperPod cluster or a training job.
One moment of a recorded episode as training reads it: the camera images and joint angles, paired with the actions that followed.
A resource saturates when the work asks it for as much per second as it can deliver. After that point, the job cannot go faster on that machine.
A lower price in exchange for a commitment to a steady amount of compute use. They lower the cost of capacity you run anyway, but they do not reserve capacity.
The Slurm command that submits a shell script as a job and returns at once.
A compute environment with a floor of 0 vCPUs, which holds no instance when its queue is empty.
The time, set with minScaleDownDelayMinutes, that Batch keeps an instance after its last job so the next job skips the launch.
The PCS setting for how long a node may sit idle before PCS removes it. The default is 600 seconds.
An optional PCS log that records each node as LAUNCHED, REGISTERED, ACTIVE or TERMINATED, together with a reason.
A simulated copy of a real place, built from a video. Splats give its appearance, and a mesh gives the surfaces that objects collide with.
SEAR's grading rule. A separate process receives the frozen policy, holds the start states and the grading code, and ignores any success that the policy claims.
A 2026 benchmark that runs coding agents on simulated and real robot tasks and grades them with a sealed judge.

Arm's counters that split a top-down share into its causes. For example, STALL_BACKEND_MEMBOUND, counted together with STALL_BACKEND, separates back-end stalls caused by memory from those caused in the core. Our runs did not count them.
The integration rule that updates the speed first and then moves the position with the new speed.

A comparison that is checked after each pair of trials and stops as soon as the evidence is sufficient. It is built so that the repeated checks do not raise the false-alarm rate. STEP (2025) proposes one for robot policies.
The single data line that the six servos share with the host. On this bus, each servo answers to its own ID.
The Batch object that puts a Batch queue in front of training jobs that Amazon SageMaker runs.
A motor, a gearbox, an encoder and a microcontroller in one box. It holds the angle that it was last given.
A small JSON document for each thing, kept in the cloud. It holds the desired state, the reported state and the difference between them.
A shadow ray is a ray sent from a point on a surface toward a light. If something blocks it, the point is in shadow.
A job described by its duration, coupling and interruptibility (section 20).
A label on a job saying whose work it is, used by fair-share scheduling.
The false-alarm rate that a comparison accepts when there is no gap. The 5% level means one false alarm in twenty.
A loss term that pushes a batch of latents toward an isotropic Gaussian. It tests the projections of the batch onto random directions.
The signal that asks a process to stop; a pod receives it when it is evicted and has its grace period to finish.
The Unix signals that ask a process to stop and that force it to stop; Batch sends them 30 seconds apart when a job times out.
Moving a policy that was trained in simulation onto the real robot.
The difference between what a simulator produces and what the real robot and its surroundings produce. It covers physics, appearance and timing.
A 2024 suite for scoring real-robot policies in simulation.
The GPU's general execution path, which does not use the tensor cores.

The GPU's general floating-point path on the ordinary CUDA cores, as opposed to the tensor pipeline. SIMT stands for single instruction, multiple threads. We read a kernel name that contains simt as a kernel that did its arithmetic on this path.
Replaying a few demonstrations recorded in a simulator from new object positions, and keeping the candidates that succeed in the physics simulation.
A program that computes how the arm and the objects around it move, so that an attempt needs no hardware.
A variant of the replay tool in Isaac Lab. It uses a GPU motion planner to plan a collision-free motion between skill segments.
One chance, in one clock cycle, to pass one micro-operation from the front end to the back end. A core has a fixed number of slots per cycle.
An open-source job scheduler for clusters. AWS's HPC test on Spot Instances ran under Slurm.
The Slurm daemon that runs on each compute node and takes orders from the controller.
The core processing unit of an NVIDIA GPU. A card has many SMs, and SM activity is the fraction of time they had work.
The fraction of time during which at least one group of threads was active on a GPU's SMs, averaged over all SMs. Threads waiting on memory count as active.
A small vision-language-action model, from the policy family covered in section 5.
A technique in which one physical core presents itself as two hardware threads, so that it can interleave two programs on the same execution units.
The Playground task that trains an SO-101 vision policy in simulation to pick a cube up. The policy is then deployed zero-shot.
A set of learned vectors that is fed to the model for one robot type. X-VLA uses soft prompts to serve many robot bodies.
The Pearson calculation applied to rank positions. It measures whether two ways of scoring put a set of policies in the same order.
Fetching and executing the instructions after a branch on a guess, before the core knows which way the branch goes.

The section of a kernel profile that reports compute and memory throughput. Each figure is the highest of the percentages reported by the counters behind it, so it need not be a share of the chip's peak arithmetic rate or memory bandwidth.
Spot Instances are spare EC2 capacity that AWS can reclaim from a running job.
Spare EC2 capacity that AWS can take back. AWS sends a warning two minutes before it does, on a best-effort basis.
EC2 taking a Spot instance back, announced two minutes before on a best-effort basis.
The warning EC2 sends two minutes, on a best-effort basis, before it takes a Spot instance back.
