A number from 1 to 10 for how likely a Spot request is to succeed in a Region or zone.
The Slurm command that lists jobs and shows the state of each one.
The Slurm command that starts a program on every node that a job was given.
The AWS service whose sessions give shell access to an instance without SSH.
One of the eight steps that an episode passes through in the loop. One stage can contain several workloads.

In a fleet, the spread of a new policy version across the arms a few at a time. The rate grows as arms are notified or succeed, and a rule cancels the arms that are still queued once too many fail. Earlier sections use rollout for one run of a policy on one arm.
The torque a motor produces when it is held still at full power. The servo datasheet gives this figure as the servo's strength.
The Arm event that counts the cycles the front end spent recovering from a flush. The formulas for the Neoverse V3, Cortex-X925 and Cortex-A725 use it.
The Arm event that counts empty slots. It is the sum of STALL_SLOT_FRONTEND and STALL_SLOT_BACKEND.
A small test program that is measured in place of the real one, such as a MuJoCo humanoid in place of the arm, or matrix-vector products in place of a policy.
The state of a job that has been placed on an instance while its container image is pulled; it sits outside the timeout.
The full description of a simulated scene at one instant. It holds every joint angle and joint speed, plus the position, orientation and motion of each loose object.
The model's description of the whole scene at one instant. Section 3 uses the word more narrowly, for observation.state, the six measured joint angles.
Inputs given to the policy as numbers, such as joint angles and object positions, with no image.
A simulated environment that steps the physics and gives the policy the joint and object states directly, with no simulated camera. It is the cheapest kind of environment to run.

In ENPIRE, one robot with its own workstation and coding agent. ENPIRE scales its fleet by adding whole stations. Each station has two robot arms, three cameras, one workstation with one GPU, and one coding agent. The fleet has eight stations.
One update of a model's weights during training. Each step is computed from one batch.
A force that changes quickly with position or speed. The integrator holds it at its start-of-step value for the whole timestep, so a large timestep can make the simulation unstable.
An instruction to treat a value as a constant during training, so that the loss does not change any weight that produced the value.
A Greengrass component that queues data on the device and exports it in the background, including files to Amazon S3.
A recorder option that encodes frames while they are captured. Without it, the recorder writes each frame as a PNG image and encodes the episode after it ends.
LeRobot's mode that trains from a dataset without downloading it first. Hugging Face reports 2.1 to 2.5 times more samples per second from four workers.
A helper agent that a coding agent starts to study one line of work in parallel.
A Greengrass deployment that targets a smaller group of devices inside the group of a parent deployment.
One of the physics steps that the simulator runs between two decisions of the policy. The SO-101 vision pick-cube task runs 20 substeps per decision.

Code that returns pass or fail for one attempt. The ENPIRE paper calls it the verifier. Its verdict is the grade that the agent works to raise. In ENPIRE, the agent writes the check once together with a person, and the check is then frozen.
The number of rollouts that ended with the task done, divided by the total number of rollouts.
A software encoder for AV1 that runs on CPU cores. Its name in LeRobot's settings is libsvtav1.
Running the policy inside the control loop. The loop blocks until the action is computed, so the arm stops during each call.
LeRobot's default mode. The arm stands still each time the policy computes its next chunk.
NVIDIA's name for the fast side of a robot model: the action head, which turns the slow side's output and the robot's state into actions.
NVIDIA's name for the slow side of a robot model: the vision-language model that reads the scene and the instruction.
Fitting a simulator's parameters to recordings of the real robot until the simulated motion matches the measured motion.
A Kubernetes mark on a node that keeps pods off unless they tolerate it; Batch taints the EKS nodes it manages.
A taint marks a node so that only pods declaring a matching toleration may be scheduled on it.
The copy of the encoder that sees the whole clip and supplies the target latents. It receives no gradient and follows the context encoder through an EMA.
HyperPod's multi-team layer on EKS: an add-on that installs Kueue and adds a cluster policy and per-team compute allocations.
The Linux command that pins a program to chosen cores. Pinning makes sure the counters come from one known core type.
Training a predictor so that every guess starts from the true history and never from its own earlier guesses.
The Jetson's always-on monitor. It reports the GPU's activation time, the memory bandwidth in use at the memory controller and the power drawn on each power rail.
Controlling a robot by hand. On the SO-101, a person moves a leader arm, and the follower arm copies its movements.

ACT's method of calling the policy on every tick, so that chunks overlap, and sending the arm a weighted average of the overlapping predictions. It gives smoother motion but costs one forward pass per tick.
One more user that submits jobs to shared hardware. A coding agent is a tenant that asks for a GPU in bursts and consumes tokens steadily.
The fraction of cycles during which the GPU's tensor pipeline was active.
GPU units that only do matrix arithmetic. Training and inference use them.
A number format that stores 10 mantissa bits where float32 stores 23. PyTorch may use it for a float32 matrix multiply when the precision setting is "high".
NVIDIA's inference compiler. It was the fastest option in NVIDIA's GR00T N1.7 benchmark table for the Jetson Orin.
NVIDIA's runtime for serving large models.
The time Kubernetes gives a pod to stop after it is told to; the window in which a training script can write a last checkpoint.
A local Greengrass server that exchanges the device certificate for temporary AWS credentials, so that no access key is stored on the device.

A small program used in place of a real policy to show how to estimate a bottleneck by hand. It multiplies a vector by six 1024 x 1024 float32 weight matrices in turn, on one CPU core. Its numbers describe the program, not a real policy.
MuJoCo's timing tool. It runs a model for 10,000 steps by default and prints the CPU time and the contact and constraint counts. With --nthread, it runs one world per thread.
The record of one device in AWS IoT.
A named set of things. A deployment to a whole fleet targets a thing group.
The amount of work a job finishes in a given time. Jobs without a deadline are sized by throughput.
One period of the arm's control clock. Its length is the control period, which is 33.3 ms at LeRobot's default rate of 30 ticks per second.
Tiled rendering draws the camera of every environment into its own tile of one large GPU image in a single pass. The image is then cut into a tensor that the policy reads directly in GPU memory.
TiledCamera is Isaac Lab's camera sensor class that draws the camera of every environment in one tiled pass. It scales to several thousand environments.
Several pods taking turns on one GPU, with no memory or compute isolation.
The amount of simulated time that one physics step advances. It is 2 ms by default in MuJoCo and 5 ms in the SO-101 pick-cube task.
The core's cache of address translations. A pointer chase over a large area also pays for its misses.
One vector that a transformer processes. An image patch or a piece of a word becomes one token.
One element of the sequence that a transformer processes. Here it is a vector made from the pixels of one tubelet.
The Greengrass component that exchanges the device certificate for short-lived AWS credentials, which other components then use.
An action chunk written as discrete tokens, so that a language model can predict them one at a time.
A method from a 2014 Intel paper. It sorts every slot of every cycle into one of four buckets to show how a core used its capacity.
PyTorch's own compiler. It is one of the three runtimes in NVIDIA's GR00T N1.7 latency table.
The PyTorch setting that decides whether a float32 matrix multiply may be computed in a narrower format. The default, "highest", keeps float32, and "high" allows TensorFloat32.
The PyTorch project's video decoder. LeRobot runs it on the CPU by default.
The largest torque the simulated servo may apply, 2.94 N m. It is set from the 12 V servo's stall torque, and the fit does not change it.
LeRobot's RTC mode for checkpoints trained with training-time RTC. The first actions of the chunk, taken from the old chunk, are fed to the model, and no guidance runs at run time.
Training frames per second is the throughput figure in Isaac Lab's benchmark. It counts the simulated frames that a training run processes per second, including the time spent updating the policy.
A SageMaker reservation of P or Trainium capacity for 1 to 182 days, which you can book up to 8 weeks ahead.
The published configuration of a training run. It sets the model, the batch size, the number of steps and which weights train.
In the VLA recipes, one round of collecting attempts and updating the model. It is a much larger unit than a control step.
A later method that trains the model with a random delay and gives it the first actions without noise, so that no guidance and no backward pass are needed at run time.
AWS's own training chip, sold as the trn instance types.
The Kubeflow Trainer object a user submits; it points at an administrator's runtime template.
To decode a video and encode it again, usually in a different codec or as separate clips.
A way of using a video model that takes a text prompt and a control video and writes a new video with the same geometry and a different appearance.
The record of one step: the observation, the action, the reward and the next observation.
The time a command takes to travel over the serial link to the servos.
A loop that streams through arrays larger than the caches. It measures memory bandwidth.
A patch extended through time: the same square in 2 consecutive frames. Each tubelet becomes one token.
The measured round trip of one remote policy request, from encoding through the network and inference to decoding.
A P6e-GB200 or P6e-GB300 machine that joins many GPUs with NVLink.
A project from 2024 that introduced recording demonstrations with a hand-held gripper and a camera, without a robot.
One pool of physical memory that both the CPU and the GPU use, so the GPU does not get all of it.

What one job in the robot's learning loop hands to the next job, such as a decoded frame, a simulation step, a training sample or an action. You count units of work per second to compare two machines.
Units of work per second divided by the watts that a machine draws under load. It tells you how much work the machine does with a fixed amount of energy.
The time the GPU takes for one training step on a batch. LeRobot's hardware guide reports it as update_s, next to the data-loading time, dataloading_s.
The USD-Camera is the highest-fidelity camera type in the Isaac Lab paper. It runs out of memory beyond 48 cameras on a 96 GB card.
The script that an EC2 instance runs when it boots. In this section, it mounts the shared file system.
Meta's video JEPA from 2025. Its encoder is pretrained on video by predicting the latents of masked regions.
Meta's latent world model that takes actions as input. It is a frozen video encoder plus a trained predictor, and it is used for planning.
The successor encoder family, released in March 2026. It is trained with a revised recipe and comes in sizes up to 2B parameters.
An encoder and a decoder that are trained together, so that the decoder can rebuild the pixels from the encoder's much smaller grid of numbers.

An open-loop score that runs the policy as it runs on the arm on each held-out frame and compares its action with the recorded action, usually as an MSE. It is meaningful only when the number of diffusion steps is held fixed.
The training objective computed on demonstrations that were held out of training. For a diffusion policy, it is the error in predicting the added noise. It is an open-loop score.
A second model that looks at the current moment of an attempt and predicts how well the attempt will end.
How far the values of one dimension spread around their average across a batch. It is 0 when every input gives the same value.
A LeRobot encoder setting that picks the first hardware encoder the recording computer offers. It falls back to SVT-AV1 when there is none.
The unit in which EC2 counts an instance's CPU capacity. On the eight-GPU sizes in this section, 24 vCPUs are 12 physical cores.
The tegrastats rail that feeds the whole Jetson board. Read this rail to get the power of the whole board.
The network's output for every possible noisy chunk: which way each number should move, and how fast.

expansion: named after its terms: variance, invariance, covariance
meaning: A method from 2022 that prevents collapse with loss terms that keep every latent dimension spread out and uncorrelated with the others.
Fixed circuits on a GPU that only compress and decompress video.
The part of the backbone that turns camera images into vectors.
A model that takes both images and text as input. In world-model evaluation, it judges whether the generated rollout completed the task.
The difference between how simulated images and real camera images look.
A transformer that reads an image as a sequence of patches, with one token per patch.
A policy built on a network that takes camera images and a text instruction as input and outputs actions.
A network pretrained on images and text from the web. It takes pictures and a prompt as input and writes text.
The private network in AWS that an EKS cluster lives in.
The textbook interval, p plus or minus z times sqrt(p(1-p)/n). It can run past 100%, and it shrinks to zero width at a perfect score.
Warp is NVIDIA's framework for writing GPU code in Python. MuJoCo Warp and the Newton Warp renderer are built on it.
On a humanoid, a small network that turns the plan into joint targets many times a second.
A core's number of slots per cycle, for example 10 on the Cortex-X925 and Neoverse V3 and 5 on the Cortex-A725.
A method for computing a confidence interval on a success rate. It pulls the centre toward one half and keeps the width above zero at 0% and 100%. LeRobot's evaluation tool reports it.
One of the dataloader's parallel processes. Each worker runs on CPU cores, and in LeRobot it also decodes the video.
One computing job behind the arm, with one resource as its bottleneck. Teaching the arm one task involves fifteen of them.

A group of jobs that behave the same way when they lose their machine. It is defined by three properties: duration, coupling and interruptibility. The five workload types are Independent tasks, Long single-machine runs, Multi-node training, Always-on streams and Real-time on the robot.
One independent copy of the simulated scene, with its own state. A GPU simulator advances thousands of worlds in one batch.
A model that predicts future video and the action chunk together. It forecasts what the camera will see as well as what the robot should do.
A model that predicts what the scene will look like after the robot takes an action.
One model that outputs the future video and the robot's actions together. The world model is then also the policy, and no search is needed.
Closed-loop scoring in which a video world model generates what the cameras would show after each action, and a vision-language model judges the generated video.
The identity file issued to a device when it is registered. The device uses it to prove its identity to AWS IoT.
The NVIDIA driver's numbered report of a GPU fault.
The share of replayed candidate demonstrations that pass the success check and are kept.
A publish/subscribe network protocol. LeRobot uses it to carry observations to the policy server and chunks back to the robot computer.
Filling the unused slots of a fixed-width state or action vector with zeros, so that one model can serve robots with different numbers of joints.
A policy is deployed zero-shot when it runs on the real robot with no further training on real data.
Running a policy trained in simulation on the real arm with no further training.
